Hi Sophie — looping in a few technical details here so you have direct answers for the SSQ. Short answers up front, fuller context below.

- SOC 2: our SOC 2 Type II report (attached) covers our hosted control plane services. For Private/VPC deployments we provide an addendum that documents controls that operate in the customer-managed VPC; I can include that addendum and a statement about our subservice organization coverage.

- Network isolation / air-gap: Redwood Private supports three deployment modes: (1) VPC-hosted private deployment with no public ingress (recommended), (2) VPC + private-link style peering for tightly controlled connectivity, and (3) on-prem air-gapped installs for regulated environments (air-gapped images and manual provisioning). The air-gapped option requires an on-site installer and offline handoff of signed images; it is available for customers with strict requirements.

- Key management: BYO KMS supported (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and HSM integration can be arranged for Private installs. We do not have customer-managed HSM hardware shipping by default but can integrate with customer HSM endpoints via standard PKCS#11 or KMIP bridges.

- Admin access controls: RBAC + SSO (SAML/OIDC), session audit logs, and optional bastion/proxy for admin access to control-plane components. All admin actions are logged to an audit log we can export to your SIEM.

Attached: redwood_private_vpc_deployment_diagram.pdf (high-level control/data plane boundaries), SOC2_SAAS_Report_2027.pdf (redacted where required).

I'll start populating the SSQ now; if you can confirm the preferred format (spreadsheet vs. DocuSign-enabled questionnaire) I will prioritize that.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
